title: Mapping Oncology patients' Self-reported experiences And metaphors to Identify latent fatigue Classes (MOSAIC)
summary:
Many people with cancer experience severe exhaustion, which is often referred to as “fatigue.” Feeling tired in the evening or after exertion is normal and usually goes away after getting enough sleep and rest. Fatigue, on the other hand, is a specific type of exhaustion. Those affected often feel unusually tired, weak, or drained—even without having exerted themselves beforehand. This fatigue does not simply go away with sleep or rest and can significantly impact daily life.

Those affected report a wide range of experiences. Some feel primarily physically exhausted and have little energy for everyday activities. Others describe problems with concentration or memory, difficulty motivating themselves, or the feeling that they recover only slowly from stress. Just as “cancer” is an umbrella term for many different types of cancer, “fatigue” likely encompasses many different types of fatigue. The goal of the MOSAIC study is therefore to identify different forms or “types” of fatigue in people with a recent or former cancer diagnosis. 

The MOSAIC study is an anonymous survey conducted online.  The goal is to include at least 600 people with a recent or former cancer diagnosis, who currently experience or have ever experienced fatigue. The survey includes descriptions and statements from people affected by fatigue, and participants are asked to indicate whether these descriptions reflect their personal experiences.  The responses will help us better understand and identify the different types of fatigue. This is important for tailoring treatment and support services more effectively to the needs of those affected.

interventions.name: MOSAIC is designed as a cross-sectional, anonymous, web-based survey conducted via the established German patient engagement platform fragdiepatienten.de. The study targets individuals with a prior or current diagnosis of any cancer type who have experienced cancer-related fatigue (CRF) at any point

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Self-reported current or past diagnosis of any cancer type
- Individuals at any stage of the cancer trajectory, including active treatment, remission, and long-term survivorship 
- Individuals with sufficient German language proficiency to complete the survey (The capacity to give consent should exist)
- Experiencing or having experienced fatigue
Exclusion criteria:
- not able to complete the survey online via smartphone, PC, or tablet
